_note: All data points are third-party published estimates or disclosures. No fabricated values. Each entry carries its source. Compiled 2026-08-11.

jegham_v6.source: Jegham, Abdelatti, Elmoubarki, Hendawi, 'How Hungry is AI?', arXiv:2505.09598v6 (2025-11-24)
jegham_v6.method: Black-box API latency proxy; assumed DGX H100/H200 nodes, batch 8; Anthropic/AWS multipliers PUE 1.14, WUE 0.18 on-site + 3.142 off-site L/kWh, CIF 0.385 kgCO2e/kWh

couch_2026.source: Simon P. Couch, 'Electricity use of AI coding agents' (2026-01-20)
couch_2026.method: Back-calculation anchored on Epoch AI GPT-4o estimate, scaled by Anthropic API price ratios; real Claude Code session logs (8,825 API calls)
couch_2026.models: Claude Opus 4.5 / Sonnet 4.5 via Claude Code

digital_applied_2026.method: Blog synthesis: public architecture data + ML.Energy per-FLOP measurements + assumed PUE/grid mix; self-declared error 2-3x either direction

google_2025.source: Elsworth et al. (Google), 'Measuring the environmental impact of delivering AI at Google scale', arXiv:2508.15734 (2025-08-21)
google_2025.method: Measured production fleet, May 2025; boundary: active TPU + host CPU/DRAM + idle provisioned machines + PUE 1.09; market-based carbon; on-site water only

epoch_2025.source: Epoch AI (Josh You), 'How much energy does ChatGPT use?' (2025-02-07)
epoch_2025.method: First-principles: ~100B active params MoE, H100 ~1500W incl. server overhead, 10% FLOP utilization, 70% peak power

oviedo_2026.source: Oviedo et al. (Microsoft), 'Energy Use of AI Inference', Joule 2026; arXiv:2509.20241
oviedo_2026.method: Production-grounded simulation, >200B-param frontier serving on H100 fleet, realistic utilization + PUE

mistral_2025.source: Mistral AI LCA with Carbone 4 / ADEME, peer-reviewed (2025-07-22)

ml_energy.source: Chung et al., ML.ENERGY Benchmark (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv:2505.06371); longitudinal blog 2025-12; Leaderboard v3.0 paper arXiv:2601.22076 (2026-01)

samsi_2023.source: Samsi et al., 'From Words to Watts', IEEE HPEC 2023, arXiv:2310.03003
samsi_2023.note: 2023 stack (V100/A100, no continuous batching); upper bound, obsolete

bloom.source: Luccioni et al., JMLR 24 (2023), arXiv:2211.02001; measured

llama31_405b.source: Meta Llama 3.1 model card (disclosed GPU-hours & tCO2e; energy derived at 700W TDP, no PUE)

external_estimate.source: SINK Project scorecard (external estimate, methodology not public)

epoch_training_flop.source: Epoch AI, 'Over 30 AI models trained at GPT-4 scale' (2025-06)

hawesville_ky.grid: MISO via Big Rivers Electric + Kenergy

avert_2023.source: EPA, 'Emission Rates from AVERT' (April 2024 release), data year 2023; sheet '2023', Regional Emission Rates, column 'Uniform EE'
avert_2023.method: Short-run marginal (avoided) CO2 rates from AVERT's hourly dispatch model, assuming 0.5% displacement of existing regional demand. 'Uniform EE' = flat all-hours load profile, the closest published match to a 24/7 data-center load. T&D-loss adjusted (retail-level) per the workbook README.
avert_2023.units: lb CO2/MWh as published; gCO2/kWh derived at 453.59237 g/lb
caveats: AVERT regions are aggregations of balancing authorities and are NOT coextensive with eGRID subregions; the ratios above cross geographic boundaries.
Indiana is split 21% Mid-Atlantic / 79% Midwest (EPA state apportionment, 2018 sales). New Carlisle is served by Indiana Michigan Power, a PJM member, placing it in the Mid-Atlantic region.

AVERT's New York region spans all of NYISO including gas-heavy downstate, while eGRID NYUP is upstate only; the 4.32x ratio is inflated by this mismatch and is not purely a marginal-vs-average effect.
EPA states AVERT 'is a marginal emissions assessment tool and not a tool for emissions accounting' and cautions against its use in corporate GHG reporting.
T&D adjustment makes these rates modestly high for a transmission-connected campus.

pjm_emissions_2022.source: PJM Interconnection, '2018-2022 CO2, SO2 and NOX Emission Rates' (April 27, 2023), Table 2
pjm_emissions_2022.method: Marginal rate = mathematical average of the emission rates of the LMP-setting unit(s) in each 5-minute dispatch interval, averaged monthly. System average = generation-weighted across all PJM generation.
pjm_emissions_2022.verified: Values read directly from the report PDF, 2026-08-11
pjm_emissions_2022.derivation: On-peak = non-holiday weekdays 07:00-23:00 = 80 of 168 h/week (0.4762); flat 24/7 load weight = 0.4762*1041 + 0.5238*976 = 1007 lb/MWh; ratio to 811 system average = 1.24x
pjm_emissions_2022.series_status: Discontinued after this edition. PJM's Reports & Notices library lists no emissions report for data years 2023-2025 as of 2026-08-11; PJM now publishes marginal emission rates via Data Miner and an interactive Emissions page instead.

iea.source: IEA Energy and AI (2025-04) + Key Questions update (2026)
